newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Tenaga plans 500 kv line to boost grid.
newsitem.headline: Tenaga plans 500 kv line to boost grid.

text.p: Malaysia's national power utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd will boost its power distribution system with a new 500-kilovolt line linking the northern and southern parts of the country, its executive chairman said.

"The 500 kv transmission lines will strengthen the national grid by increasing the efficiency of power transmission between the northern and southern parts of the country," the daily New Straits Times quoted Ahmad Tajudin Ali as saying.
The newspaper said Tenaga was in the process of completing a 630 million ringgit 500-kv transmission line from Pasir Gudang to Yong Peng in the southern part of peninsular Malaysia.
Construction on the Pasir Gudang-Yong Peng section began early this year and would be completed by next year, it said quoting the Tenaga chairman.
This would link up with a similar line between Kapar and Gurun in the northern region being planned by the company. Kapar would then be connected to Yong Peng, Tajudin said.
The total project would cost two billion ringgit, he said.
"This (new line) is necessary in the event of having to transmit very high voltages of power," Tajudin said.
Tenaga has said it would upgrade its power distribution system after an embarrassing nationwide blackout in August.
